findings.evidence: Intro paragraph restates the description: 'Turn a Markdown document with embedded mermaid diagrams into a PDF (or a marp deck) in one non-destructive command...'
findings.fix: Cut the intro to one line naming the one fact the description lacks: rendering runs on a temp copy and feeds the best complete pipeline.

findings.evidence: 'Draft or final? Iterating → any installed backend is fine. Final → let the quality-ranked auto-selection pick' gives the same action (run the script with no flags) for both branches
findings.fix: Replace the draft/final question with one that changes what the agent does, for example 'Does the user name a backend? Only then pass --backend', or delete the question.

findings.evidence: 'NEVER nag for an install when a complete pipeline already works. All four backends are "good enough"' gives a preference, not a failure mode learned in practice
findings.fix: Swap it for a concrete gotcha, for example how mmdc/puppeteer behaves in sandboxed containers or how pandoc-latex handles relative image paths.

findings.evidence: Description has no boundary against near misses such as DOCX/HTML to PDF, editing an existing PDF, or theming an existing marp deck; the phrasing is declarative
findings.fix: Use when the user wants to turn a .md file into a PDF or a marp slide deck (pdf, pptx, html), including Markdown with ```mermaid diagrams: "export markdown to pdf", "md to pdf", "render mermaid and make a PDF", "build a deck from this markdown". Renders every mermaid block with mmdc on a temp copy (the source is never edited) and picks the best installed backend (Pandoc+LaTeX > Typst > WeasyPrint > Chromium); never auto-installs. Not for converting DOCX or HTML to PDF, editing, merging or compressing existing PDFs, rendering a lone mermaid diagram, or restyling an existing marp deck. Keywords: markdown to pdf, md to pdf, mermaid, marp deck, slide deck, pandoc, typst.

findings.evidence: examples/sample-with-mermaid.md is tracked, but neither SKILL.md nor references/backends.md references it
findings.fix: Reference it from SKILL.md with a condition ('to smoke-test the installed toolchain, run the primary flow on examples/sample-with-mermaid.md'), or delete it.

findings.evidence: 'Hand the .rendered.md to marp-slide for themes/polish/export' does not say how to clean up the .rendered.md and .rendered-assets/ that it writes beside the source
findings.fix: State where --render-only writes its output, and whether the agent removes the .rendered.md and .rendered-assets/ after the hand-off or leaves them for the user.

findings.evidence: The e2e module has 1 test. The scripts print free-form text ('Wrote ... (backend: ..., diagrams: ...)'), and detect_backends.py prints nothing when run directly
findings.fix: Add e2e coverage for the deck and --render-only paths. Add a structured output option (for example --json) to markdown_to_pdf.py and detect_backends.py, and assert on it in tests/test_markdown_to_pdf.py.

findings.evidence: Trigger query 'Which PDF backend is installed for markdown conversion on this machine?' should trigger, but no branch answers it without converting: scripts/detect_backends.py exits 0 with no output, and backends.md is reserved for 'which backend is best'
findings.fix: Add a decision row 'User asks which backend is installed' that runs a detection command printing the backend it would choose (give detect_backends.py a main that prints it), and say no file is written.

findings.evidence: The flow ends at reporting the 'Wrote ...' line; there is no check that the PDF exists, is non-empty, or has its diagrams embedded
findings.fix: Add a validation step after exit 0: confirm the output file exists and is non-empty (for example with pdfinfo when installed), and re-run with --format png if diagrams are missing.
